{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"073ef503956baf1f0527bbd06f36eeb6b09b9db93e7efd82bd4e0fd508825ccd","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:33","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Parking and stopping: parallel, angle and hill parking, disabled parking, no-parking places and distances, emergency parking","heading":"C2 — Parking confusables: uphill versus downhill wheels, the different no-parking distances, fire station sides, railroad crossing versus track distance, and breakdown exceptions","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Parking confusables: uphill versus downhill wheels, the different no-parking distances, fire station sides, railroad crossing versus track distance, and breakdown exceptions
Confusable pairs from the parking and stopping pages, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
With a curb you stay within 12 inches of it, but with no curb you simply get as close as you can to the shoulder edge, with no set number. [A01]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; confusable curb versus no curb; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
Pulling out of a parking spot, you yield to all other traffic; traffic does not have to yield to you because you signaled. [A01]
Why it matters: group leaving a parked position; confusable signaling versus yielding; difficulty easy.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A02
Facing downhill at a curb the front wheels point toward the curb, while facing uphill at a curb they point toward the travel lane. [A02]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable downhill curb versus uphill curb; difficulty hard.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A02
Without a curb, the front wheels point toward the road edge whether the vehicle faces uphill or downhill. [A02]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable curb versus no curb on a hill; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A02
On a hill the parking brake is always set, and the gear selection differs only by transmission: in gear for a manual, in park for an automatic. [A02]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable manual versus automatic; difficulty easy.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A03
The no-stopping list is waived only for a breakdown that leaves your vehicle stuck in the lanes or with no room on the shoulder, not for a short errand. [A03]
Why it matters: group no-parking exceptions; confusable breakdown versus convenience; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A03
Every place on the no-parking list, the 10-foot fire hydrant zone included, bans stopping as well as parking. [A03]
Why it matters: group no-parking list; confusable stopping versus parking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A04
Near a fire station driveway the limit is 15 feet on the same side of the street but 75 feet on the opposite side. [A04]
Why it matters: group no-parking distances; confusable same side versus opposite side; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A04
The 50-foot rule near a railroad or light rail crossing is measured from the nearest rail, while the 7 1/2-foot rule applies along any tracks only when you would interfere with a train. [A04]
Why it matters: group no-parking distances; confusable crossing distance versus track clearance; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A04
The 50-foot rule near a traffic signal or sign applies only when your vehicle would hide it from view, unlike the railroad crossing rule of the same distance, which always applies. [A04]
Why it matters: group no-parking distances; confusable signal or sign versus railroad crossing; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A04
Hazard lights are the warning for any breakdown stop, and when the vehicle cannot be seen from 200 feet each way you add warning devices set at least 200 feet out in both directions. [A04]
Why it matters: group emergency parking; confusable visible versus hidden breakdown; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A04
A police officer can remove a vehicle parked where parking is banned or one creating a hazard, and you are the one responsible for the towing and storage costs. [A04]
Why it matters: group towing; confusable removal by police versus cost to owner; difficulty easy.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]
